result.summary: The intersection features wide multi-lane roadways with high-visibility crosswalks but lacks pedestrian refuge islands, leading to long exposure times. Large vehicles and a car-centric design create a challenging environment for pedestrians despite the presence of basic infrastructure like sidewalks and curb ramps.

hazards.name: Long Crossing Distance
hazards.description: Pedestrians must cross multiple lanes of traffic without a refuge island, increasing exposure time.

hazards.name: Sightline Obstruction
hazards.description: Large vehicles, like the white truck in the foreground, can block the view between drivers and pedestrians.
hazards.location_in_image: Left foreground where the white truck is positioned

interventions.title: Pedestrian Refuge Island
interventions.description: Install a raised median island to allow pedestrians to cross one direction of traffic at a time.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions
interventions.description: Extend the sidewalk into the roadway to shorten crossing distance and improve visibility between pedestrians and drivers.

result.summary: The intersection is equipped with high-visibility continental crosswalk markings, curb ramps with tactile paving, and pedestrian signals. However, the wide roadway with multiple travel lanes increases pedestrian exposure and suggests a higher-speed traffic environment in an industrial-commercial area.

hazards.name: Long Crossing Distance
hazards.description: The wide roadway requires pedestrians to be exposed to traffic for a significant duration without a refuge.
hazards.location_in_image: Across the main roadway at the marked crosswalk

hazards.name: Multiple Threat Risk
hazards.description: Multiple lanes of traffic traveling in the same direction can lead to visibility issues where one vehicle stops for a pedestrian but another in an adjacent lane does not.

interventions.title: Pedestrian Refuge Island
interventions.description: Install a raised median island to allow pedestrians to cross the wide roadway in two stages.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions
interventions.description: Construct bulb-outs to shorten the crossing distance and improve the visibility between drivers and pedestrians.

interventions.title: Leading Pedestrian Interval
interventions.description: Adjust signal timing to give pedestrians a head start before vehicles receive a green light.

result.summary: The image depicts a pedestrian crossing at a wide signalized entrance to an industrial or commercial lot. While the crossing features marked crosswalks and tactile curb ramps, the environment is dominated by large vehicle infrastructure and lacks visible pedestrian-specific signals.

hazards.name: Wide Curb Radii
hazards.description: The wide entrance allows for high-speed vehicle turns across the pedestrian path.
hazards.location_in_image: The junction where the driveway meets the main sidewalk

hazards.name: Visual Obstruction
hazards.description: Chain-link fencing and parked trucks inside the lot may obscure pedestrians from the view of exiting drivers.
hazards.location_in_image: Left side of the driveway entrance

hazards.name: Lack of Pedestrian Signals
hazards.description: Despite the presence of traffic lights for vehicles, there are no visible pedestrian signal heads to indicate when it is safe to cross.

interventions.title: Install Pedestrian Signals
interventions.description: Add countdown pedestrian signal heads to provide clear right-of-way information for people crossing the driveway.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions / Radius Tightening
interventions.description: Reduce the turning radius at the entrance to slow down vehicles and shorten the pedestrian crossing distance.

interventions.title: Daylighting and Sightline Improvements
interventions.description: Ensure the area near the sidewalk is clear of fencing or parked vehicles that block visibility between drivers and pedestrians.
